segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus once told a story about two men who lived side by side, yet worlds apart.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One was rich. He wore the finest purple and linen, and every day of his life was a feast.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Just outside his house, at his own gate, lay a poor beggar named Lazarus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was covered in sores, and so hungry he only wished for the scraps that fell from the rich man's table. Even the stray dogs came and licked his wounds.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The rich man walked past that gate every single day. And every day he stepped around the suffering man lying there, and did nothing.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the day came that comes for us all. Lazarus died — and the angels carried him home, to Abraham's side, into light and comfort at last.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The rich man died too, and was buried. But he opened his eyes in a place of torment: a dark and thirsty place, far from the light.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Across a vast divide he could see Abraham in the distance, with Lazarus resting beside him. And he cried out, begging for just a drop of water to cool his tongue.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And between them, Abraham said, a great gulf had been fixed — one that no one could ever cross.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the rich man begged again: then send someone to my five brothers, to warn them, so they never come to this place.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They already have the writings of Moses and the prophets, Abraham replied. Let them listen. But the man pleaded — no, if only someone came back from the dead, then they would turn.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Abraham gave his final answer.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus told this to people who had everything, and walked right past the ones who had nothing. It was a warning — but underneath it, a mercy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Because the day is still yours — for now.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There is a gate before you today, and someone waiting at it. Who are you walking past — and will you stop while there is still time?
